fair_value.method: Blend at Oct-2027: site-by-site split-rate FCFF DCF $2.6 (50%; contracted cash flows at 6.75-10%, everything else at 11%; single-rate $1.1); 7.5x NTM EBITDA $5.8bn less $23.2bn net debt over 554M shares $36.6 (40%); 1.0x diluted book $10.4 (10%). Weighted $17.0.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-by-site quarterly FCFF, FY27-FY60, terminal on the last refresh cycle at WACC (g 2.5%). Split-rate discounting: cash flows inside signed contract terms at counterparty rates (Microsoft 6.75%, NVIDIA 7.0%, non-IG AI developers 10.0%); post-contract, uncontracted, pipeline, corporate and terminal at WACC 11%. Contracted (S01 Microsoft 200MW IT at $9.7M/MW-yr, H1 from Aug-26 and H2-4 from Feb-27, 5 yrs; S07 Prince George 28MW, $0.5bn ARR, 2-yr terms; S08 Mackenzie 44MW and S02 Childress 28MW at $21.7M/MW, 3 yrs from Jan-27; S03 NVIDIA 43MW IT (60MW gross) $0.68bn/yr, 5 yrs from Apr-27, Dell GPUs $1.6bn). Uncontracted under construction, probability-weighted (S04 Childress air 135MW p=0.80 from Jul-27; S09 Canal Flats 21MW p=0.75; S05 Horizons 5-6 100MW p=0.75 from Jan-28; S10 Sweetwater 1 ph1 200MW p=0.65 from Apr-28): success at $20M/MW for 3 yrs, failure = contract 18 months late at $17M; data-center capex spent in both branches, GPU capex follows the contract. Pipeline (S11-S16, 3,060MW IT announced, 1,155MW expected): phased 2029-33 builds at $18M/MW 3-yr terms, $34M GPU + $11.7M infra per MW, probabilities 0.20-0.50, plus $3.8bn of development spend (FY27 $0.8bn + $2.0bn guide gap, FY28 $1.0bn) charged regardless. GPU economics: contract price for the term; then market rent by vintage = $20M/MW new-contract level x 0.85 glut haircut x age index (1.00, 0.92, 0.82, 0.72, 0.64, 0.58, 0.52, 0.46 ...); EBITDA = 80% of revenue less $1.6M/MW-yr power+site (owned sites, no colocation rent) in and after the term; idle if negative; refresh at 6 years at current GPU cost per MW ($34M liquid / $40M air-cooled, i.e. 17% above Microsoft's $29M) less 9% salvage, re-contract at $17M for 3 yrs. Corporate $0.25bn/yr +4%. Revenue FY27 $2.8bn, FY28 $8.5bn, FY29 $11.4bn; EBITDA $1.6/5.7/7.7bn; capex $22.8/10.2/11.5bn (FY27 $24.1bn if every 2027 site contracts on time). EV $2.6bn less adjusted net debt $1.62bn over 444M diluted shares = $2.2 today, x1.146 = $2.6 at Oct-2027. Single 11% rate: $1.1. Life (split, Oct-27): 4y -19.8, 5y -4.2, 6y 2.6, 7y 6.0, 8y 7.1. Sensitivities (Oct-27): no glut haircut (H=1.0) 41.9; H=0.75 -23.7; tails +30% 32.2; WACC 10% 14.4 / 12% -6.9; refresh at 0.9x 14.1 / 1.1x -9.0; 4-yr refresh contracts 11.5; 2027 sites at $25M 8.5; pipeline at $20M 8.5 / $16M -3.3; no pipeline and no guide-gap spend -1.5; probabilities x0.6 -3.1 / x1.3 6.7; new-contract level $22M 24.9 / $18M -19.8; no salvage -10.5.

inputs_detail.value: 200MW IT at $9.7M/MW-yr ($1.94bn/yr), 5-yr terms; H1 50MW from Aug-2026, H2-4 150MW from Feb-2027; remaining capex $5.4bn in FY27 (GPU $4.4bn + data center $1.0bn)
inputs_detail.derivation: TCV $9.7bn / 5 yrs / 200MW (inventory S01). H1 accepted Aug-2026; H2-4 targeted Q4 CY2026 with grace to start of Q2 2027, so I use Feb-2027 (judgment, midpoint). GPU capex $5.81bn and ~$3bn data centers per inventory; the FY27 remainder split is my estimate. The 20% prepayment stays debt-like in net debt; per the 10-K only $1,013m of the $1.843bn deferred revenue sits in the Microsoft SPV (inventory F11), the rest is other customers' prepayments, still treated as debt-like.

inputs_detail.value: 100MW IT: Prince George 28MW at $0.5bn ARR (2-yr terms, live now); Mackenzie 44MW and Childress air 28MW at $21.7M/MW (3-yr from Jan-2027); remaining GPU capex $3.9bn + $0.3bn retrofit
inputs_detail.derivation: Inventory: 2026 program 480MW gross / ~300MW IT, ~$4bn ARR excluding NVIDIA; less Microsoft $1.94bn = $2.06bn on ~100MW IT. Prince George ARR conflicts ($0.4bn release vs $0.5bn Q3 footnote): I use $0.5bn, the latest and the one that matches the 'just under $500m' call remark. IT MW split by gross MW. Mackenzie GPU capex $2.7bn implied by the $2.4bn 9% financing at 90%; Childress B300 remainder ~$0.8bn of the $3.5bn order. Terms: portfolio weighted-average ~4 yrs including the 5-yr Microsoft/NVIDIA contracts implies ~2.7 yrs for the rest; recent contracts are 3-yr.

inputs_detail.value: 43MW IT (60MW gross), $0.68bn/yr for 5 years from Apr-2027; Dell GPUs $1.6bn paid on shipment plus $0.2bn retrofit
inputs_detail.derivation: $3.4bn TCV / 5 yrs. The Q3 call says the 60MW is part of a 250MW retrofit of 'existing air-cooled capacity' inside a 400MW gross Childress 2027 plan, so I treat 60MW as gross and convert at the 0.71 IT/gross ratio implied by 0.8GW IT on 1.21GW gross; this resolves the inventory's open IT-vs-gross point. Fixes flag F04: modelled as its own contracted cohort at contract terms and early-2027 timing instead of inside the generic 2027 build at 4 yrs from mid-FY28.

inputs_detail.value: 456MW IT (135 + 100 + 21 + 200); success p = 0.80 / 0.75 / 0.75 / 0.65 at $20M/MW, 3 yrs; failure = 18 months later at $17M; capex $45M/MW air retrofit, $42M Canal Flats, $49M new liquid
inputs_detail.derivation: 0.8GW IT by end-2027 less 300MW 2026 and 43MW NVIDIA leaves 456MW. Probabilities: 2026 capacity contracted ahead of commissioning and management cites late-stage talks at ~$25M/MW (company, seller-interested), so high but below 1; Sweetwater 1 lowest because its Batch Zero allocation is conditional until spring 2027 and GPUs are not ordered. Price at the low end of the >$20M disclosed range. GPU capex: $40M/MW air-cooled B300 ($3.5bn for >50k B300) and $34M/MW liquid rack-scale (Microsoft GB300 $29M plus the CFO's 15-20% per-MW inflation); infrastructure $5M air retrofit, $8M Canal Flats, $15M new liquid ($14-16M per Microsoft investor update).

inputs_detail.value: Sweetwater 1 rest 733MW IT p=0.50; Sweetwater 2 400 p=0.40; Kiowa 1,067 p=0.35; Bundey 533 p=0.30; Badajoz 200 p=0.35; other Spain 127 p=0.20; phased 2029-33; $18M/MW 3-yr; $34M GPU + $11.7M infra per MW; $3.8bn development spend charged regardless
inputs_detail.derivation: Gross MW from the inventory converted at IREN's 2:3 IT/gross design ratio. Probability basis: energized substation and conditional Batch Zero Base Load for Sweetwater 1 (highest); Sweetwater 2 substation not yet energized; Kiowa grid studies complete but 1.6GW is large against funding capacity; Bundey needs regulatory approvals; Spain in permitting; other Spain undisclosed. Pipeline pricing 10% below today's $20M for deflation. Development spend: FY27 $0.8bn plus the $2.0bn gap between my bottom-up FY27 capex and the $25bn low end of the guide, FY28 $1.0bn; infra per MW reduced by the $3.3M/MW of expected MW already spent. Kiowa connection right cost $105m and Nostrum ~$148m (10-K) are sunk and not added back.

inputs_detail.input: Contract EBITDA and tail cash cost
inputs_detail.value: EBITDA = 80% of revenue less $1.6M per MW-yr (power ~$0.9M at $0.08/kWh x PUE 1.3, site opex ~$0.7M); same formula during and after contracts
inputs_detail.derivation: Round 3 used 80% of revenue less $2.4M/MW, which included ~$150/kW-month colocation rent; the inventory confirms IREN owns all its sites freehold, so I remove the rent. At $20M/MW this gives 72% (round 3: 68%); at Microsoft's $9.7M it gives 63%, below the company's 85% estimate. Corporate cost $0.25bn/yr growing 4% (unchanged).

inputs_detail.value: Microsoft 6.75%; NVIDIA 7.0%; non-IG contracted 10.0%; everything else 11% WACC
inputs_detail.derivation: Microsoft: the $3.65bn A-rated (Fitch A / DBRS A(low)) GPU facility secured on this contract prices at 6.00% blended (5.96% USPP, SOFR+2.25% DDTL); +75bp for completion risk on unaccepted H2-4 (delivery-date termination right) and IREN's managed-services performance risk on the equity layer. NVIDIA: AA (S&P, affirmed Aug-2026) but no financing closed yet and commissioning not started, so 6.0% + 100bp. Non-IG AI developers (unrated): Mackenzie secured paper prices at 9.0% fixed for 30-month amortizing tranches at 90% advance; the residual equity layer bears customer default risk, so +100bp, kept below WACC because 45-55% prepayments and short tenors limit exposure.
Unchanged: Ke = 5.29% 10y UST + beta 2.2 x 4.23% ERP = 14.6%; pre-tax Kd ~7.5%, 60/40 E/D. Applies to post-contract, uncontracted, pipeline, corporate and terminal flows.
Unchanged.
Unchanged: debt $7.593bn - $0.436bn ITM converts + leases $0.244bn + deferred revenue $1.843bn - cash $5.896bn - restricted cash $1.724bn (30-Jun-2026).
Unchanged.

With market-anchored tails and refresh at current cost (supervisor corrections), value in my model rises with life to a plateau at 7-8 years (aged GPUs still cover cash costs), so life is an output. I take 6: above the 5-yr book life in the 10-K (HPC hardware 5, verified; fact-check confirms CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5, IREN 5) but short of the model optimum because of failure rates on large clusters, 3-5-yr OEM support and Nvidia's yearly cadence.

Supervisor correction: anchored to the market rent for that vintage, not to the contract price. Per-MW evidence: H100 at ~3.5 yrs ~0.63 of new-generation per-MW pricing, A100 at ~6 yrs 0.37-0.51 (Silicon Data A100 $1.58, Ornn); CoreWeave says prior-gen pricing is 'at or above where it was years ago' (seller-interested). The 0.85 glut haircut (skeptic) gives a first re-lease of ~0.59 of contract for 2026 cohorts (supervisor's defensible range 0.55-0.70) and $9-10M/MW for the Microsoft GB300 cohort at age 5 (round 3: ~$4M).

inputs_detail.value: Current GPU cost per MW ($34M liquid, $40M air) at age 6, less 9% salvage of the cohort's cost; re-contract at $17M/MW for 3 yrs
inputs_detail.derivation: Supervisor correction: round 3 refreshed at 90% of original nominal cost; now at today's per-MW cost (17% above Microsoft's $29M, consistent with the CFO's 15-20% per-MW inflation). Salvage from CCIR executed medians halved for rack-scale systems (12% at 5 yrs, 9% at 6). Re-contract = $20M x 0.85.
Unchanged (equity at Ke).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 7.5x NTM EBITDA $5.8bn = EV $43.5bn, less net debt incl. prepayments $23.2bn, over 554M shares = $36.6 at Oct-2027. At 6.5x $26.2; 7.0x $31.4.

inputs_detail.derivation: Site model EBITDA for Oct-2027 to Sep-2028 $6.44bn (contracted sites including NVIDIA from Apr-2027, probability-weighted 2027 sites, owned-site cost structure), cut 10% for delivery slippage as in round 3.

CoreWeave trades ~7.5x 2027e EBITDA (MarketScreener, 1-Oct-2026). Round-3 supervisor correction: my 1x discount for short-lived GPU assets double-counted what CoreWeave's multiple already prices for the sector, so I now use the peer multiple; the customer-credit point is now handled by the split discount rates in the DCF. At my old 6.5x the value is $26.2.

$1.62bn today + FY27 FCFF burn $21.2bn (probability-weighted capex $22.8bn incl. $2.0bn guide-gap spend; $24.1bn if all 2027 sites contract on time) + Q1 FY28 burn $3.3bn + ~$1.1bn after-tax interest, less $4.0bn equity. Prepayments stay debt-like.
444M diluted + ~105M from ~$4.0bn ATM at ~$38 (inside the $4-9bn residual funding gap after $14bn committed + ~$8bn expected financing; 47.2M ATM shares already issued for ~$2.5bn) + ~5M new RSUs.

methods.inputs: Book value floor: equity $4.186bn + $0.436bn ITM convert carrying value on conversion = $4.62bn / 444M diluted shares x 1.0.

As in the DCF
Liquidation-style floor; FY26 impairments of $639m show book can fall too.

bear.story: Horizons 2-4 slip past the Q2-2027 grace window or the CY2027 build stalls; non-Microsoft customers (mostly non-IG AI labs and startups) churn or renegotiate as GPU rental prices soften (McKinsey: returns flatline below 80% utilization). The residual $4-9bn of FY27 funding comes only from 9%+ secured debt and ATM issuance in the teens, pushing shares toward 600M. Equity trades near 1.5x book. Round 3: the market starts to price the GPU-life risk itself, i.e. 2026-27 Blackwell cohorts re-leasing at ~40% of contract price after year 4 as Rubin ships, which on my 6-7-yr cases leaves the equity near zero on a DCF.

base.story: ARR reaches ~$4bn by early CY2027, a quarter late; about 400MW of the +500MW 2027 build is delivered at ~$20M/MW. Shares rise to ~550M via ATM and RSUs, and $7-9bn of prepayments sit as credits against future fees. The market pays ~7x NTM EBITDA (near CoreWeave's 7.5x) rather than my 6.5x, so the price sits well above my $17 fair value but below today: over 12 months the market prices contracted ARR and funding, not 2031 re-leasing rents, and today's evidence (H100 index firm, CoreWeave re-contracting near original price) keeps the GPU-life debate dormant.

bull.story: Clean delivery of >$4bn ARR; 2027 contracts at $20-25M/MW with 45-55% prepayments; more IG-rated financing lowers the cost of capital; Sweetwater contracts signed and neocloud multiples recover, taking the stock toward the ~$78 consensus target. GPU rents stay at today's relative levels (A100/H100 at 40-60% of new-gen per MW), validating a 6-yr-plus cash life.

thesis_break_reason: At $20 the diluted market cap is ~$9bn on 444M shares and EV is ~2.3x the $4.7bn of contracted ARR (2026 program plus NVIDIA, per the site inventory), about 31% below the $28.93 52-week low. Trading there would most likely mean a break signal: Microsoft H2-4 missing the start-of-Q2-2027 grace date, FY27 funding only on distressed terms, NVIDIA commissioning slipping well past early 2027, or failure among the unrated AI-developer customers that hold ~$2bn of ARR. Round 4: I raise it from $18 because the supervisor rightly said my cut tracked my fair value, not a break criterion. My low DCF is a long-run view of refresh economics (2031+) that cannot show up as a break within 12 months.

key_uncertainties: Post-contract and refresh pricing: the glut haircut on new-generation per-MW pricing moves the DCF from -23.7 (H=0.75) to 41.9 (H=1.0) per share; each $2M/MW on the $20M new-contract level is ~$20-25/share. Today's evidence comes from a power- and supply-constrained market.

Refresh economics: re-contracting at $17M/MW on $34-40M/MW of GPUs earns about the cost of capital, so value is earned mostly in the first contract and the aged-GPU tail; refresh at 0.9x vs 1.1x of current cost is 14.1 vs -9.0.

Contracted value is small relative to its capex: within their terms the Microsoft and 2026 cohorts roughly repay the capex still to be spent on them, so the split discount rate adds only $1.5/share; Mackenzie's 3-yr contracts do not cover its $2.7bn of GPUs.

Credit quality: about $2bn of ARR is with unrated AI developers (Perplexity, Figure AI, Together, Fluidstack and others) financed at 9% with parent guarantees; Microsoft and NVIDIA are the only IG counterparties.
Funding $23-24bn of FY27 capex and the dilution path (~444M -> ~554M shares by Oct-2027); NVIDIA's option on 30m shares at $70.
Uncontracted 2027 sites (456MW IT) and pipeline (3.1GW IT announced): probabilities are judgment; x0.6 / x1.3 moves the DCF to -3.1 / 6.7.
Execution of Microsoft Horizons 2-4 (grace to start of Q2 2027) and the delivery-date termination right.
AI demand cycle and GPU rental pricing (Silicon Data H100 $2.77, A100 $1.58; Nvidia yearly cadence and Rubin's claimed 10x cost-per-token cut argue for faster decay ahead).
reasoning: Round 4 (sites and split discounting). I rebuilt the DCF site by site from the inventory, quarterly: Microsoft (200MW IT, $9.7M, 5 yrs), the 2026 non-IG cohorts at Prince George, Mackenzie and Childress (~100MW IT, $2.06bn ARR, 2-3-yr terms, $4.2bn capex left), NVIDIA as its own contract (60MW gross = 43MW IT per the Q3 call wording, $0.68bn/yr, 5 yrs from Apr-2027; fixes F04), the four uncontracted 2027 sites probability-weighted (0.65-0.80; failure = 18 months later at $17M; data-center capex spent either way), six pipeline sites probability-weighted (0.20-0.50, 1,155 of 3,060MW IT expected) net of capex and $3.8bn of development spend, residual mining and ASIC sales, and the unannounced pipeline excluded. No MW is counted twice. I applied the round-3 supervisor's corrections: tails at market rent by vintage ($20M x 0.85 glut haircut x per-MW age index), refresh at current per-MW GPU cost, and 7.5x on EBITDA. Because IREN owns its sites I removed colocation rent from the cost structure (80% of revenue less $1.6M/MW). Results at Oct-2027: single-rate DCF $1.1, split-rate $2.6 (Microsoft 6.75% off its 6.00% A-rated facility, NVIDIA 7.0%, non-IG 10.0% off the 9% Mackenzie paper). The split adds little because within their terms contracted cash flows mostly repay the capex still to be spent on them; the value and risk sit after the contracts. Bridge (single rate): round-3 inputs in the site model $13.5 -> owned-site cost +$14 -> 3-yr terms -$14 -> refresh at current cost -$14 -> 6-yr life +$7 -> $2bn guide-gap spend -$5 -> $1.1. Life now raises value up to 7-8 yrs; I use 6. The DCF is the skeptic's number: on my central pricing (new contracts $20M, then $17M) a refresh cycle earns about WACC, so the equity is worth roughly its contracted cash plus the aged-GPU tail, less corporate cost. It is extremely sensitive to post-contract pricing (H=1.0 gives 41.9). EV/EBITDA at 7.5x is $36.6 (NTM $5.8bn, net debt $23.2bn, 554M shares). Blend 50/40/10 with book $10.4 = $17.0 (round 3 $17.2). Since fair value is about unchanged and the 12-month price still turns on Horizon 2-4 acceptance and funding, I leave the scenarios and both ladders unchanged (median ~$31.8, P(>=spot) 0.36). The thesis break goes back to $20 per the supervisor. Research this round: one re-fetch (Q3 FY26 call transcript, to settle whether NVIDIA's 60MW is gross); the rest from the site inventory, the fact-check file and earlier sources. No option prices or priors consulted.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Contract price for the contract term (2-5 yrs); afterwards market rent for the vintage = $20M/MW new-contract level x 0.85 glut haircut x age index 1.00, 0.92, 0.82, 0.72, 0.64, 0.58, 0.52, 0.46, 0.40, 0.35 (H100-at-3.5-yrs and A100-at-6-yrs per-MW evidence); EBITDA = 80% of revenue less $1.6M/MW-yr; idle if negative; refresh at 6 yrs at current GPU cost per MW ($34M liquid / $40M air) less 9% salvage, re-contract at $17M/MW for 3 yrs, then the same tail.
gpu_life.note: Split-rate values per share at Oct-2027 (single-rate: 5y -5.7, 6y 1.1, 7y 4.6; 4y -19.8, 8y 7.1). With the supervisor's two corrections (tail anchored to market by vintage instead of contract x index; refresh at current rather than 90% of original cost) the life slope reversed: longer lives now raise value up to a 7-8-yr plateau, because a refresh at $34-40M/MW re-contracted at $17M earns about the cost of capital while an aged GPU still covers its cash costs. I use 6 yrs, between the 10-K's 5-yr book life (fact-check: CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5, IREN 5) and the model optimum. Life now moves the DCF ~$3-4 per year near the base; the glut haircut on post-contract and refresh pricing dominates (H=1.0: 41.9; H=0.75: -23.7).

discounting.basis: Contract-term cash flows (EBITDA less committed capex and allocated tax) are discounted at a rate anchored on IREN's actual secured financing against that contract: Microsoft's A-rated $3.65bn GPU facility at 6.00% blended + 75bp for completion (H2-4 not yet accepted; delivery-date termination right) and managed-services performance risk on the equity layer = 6.75%; NVIDIA (AA, no facility yet, commissioning early 2027) 6.0% + 100bp = 7.0%; unrated AI developers: Mackenzie's 9.0% 30-month secured paper + 100bp for the unsecured residual = 10.0%, below WACC because of 45-55% prepayments and 2-3-yr tenors. Post-contract tails, refreshes, uncontracted and pipeline sites, corporate cost and terminal value stay at the 11% WACC. The split adds only $1.5 per share: within their terms the contracted cash flows roughly repay the GPU and data-center capex still to be spent on them (Microsoft term PV about $-1.1/share, Mackenzie $-3.0), so a lower rate on them moves little; the equity value and its risk sit in the post-contract years, which stay at WACC.
